clue.text: Money: a sort of thing that runs short?

indicators.note: something that runs short falls a little under its full length, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a kind or sort of thing

explanation.surface: A wry definition of money as the kind of thing that always runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Money is famously the thing that 'runs short', which hides that the phrase is an instruction to cut the last letter of SPECIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is coin as opposed to paper money, so it names actual metal currency.

clue.text: Certain type of pyramid? Sensible not having sex on top

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards from the clue order: 'on top' puts the second phrase first in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron, the pyramid with four triangular faces, is one of the five regular polyhedra known by this name.

clue.text: American musical, live, hosted by church group

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
to live is to be, as in 'I am'
a lot is a set or batch

explanation.surface: A Broadway show staged live by a parish group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church group' reads as one phrase, but church and group are separate pieces with AM tucked inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the Lerner and Loewe stage show about King Arthur, first produced on Broadway in 1960.

clue.text: Notorious rogue is punished around 9

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 9 down is the Latin phrase abbreviated e.g.

explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, shocking in a way that is widely known and remarked upon.

clue.text: Dutch explorer positioned to return with Queen, say

explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen, say' looks royal but points to chess, where any piece can be called a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the seventeenth-century Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand.

clue.text: What you might call Elon Musk’s remuneration?

definitions.text: What you might call Elon Musk’s remuneration?

blocks.note: surface reading: how would you describe the size of a billionaire's pay?
setter's reading: a sum so huge it has as many digits as something you dial, and 'call' hints at phoning

explanation.walkthrough: The informal British phrase for a vast sum of money is one with as many digits as a phone listing; Musk is reputedly the richest person alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, an enormous salary or price is said to run to this many figures, a long string of digits.

clue.text: Personnel regularly intervening in unhappy scrap

blocks.note: unhappy means sad
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Staff keep stepping in during an unhappy fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' usually means alternate letters; here it says the inserted pair do not stay together but alternate with the host's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken fragment of glass or pottery, a small piece or scrap of something.

clue.text: Caribbean island not supporting most of Pacific island

blocks.note: to be anti is to oppose rather than support

explanation.surface: One island in the Caribbean refuses to back another out in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: Both islands are real; only the Caribbean one is the answer, while the Pacific one loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is the larger island of the nation Antigua and Barbuda in the Leeward Islands of the West Indies.

clue.text: Upright performers in dance curtailed for royal venue

explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is the Scottish home of the British royal family, used as a summer residence.

clue.text: What might be a triple-X image, say

indicators.note: asking what something might be invites a different form made from the same letters

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as a pornographic picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triple-X' suggests an adult rating, but it is just letters for rearranging, and 'say' is used as in 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'for the sake of example', the full form of the abbreviation used where one writes 'for instance'.

clue.text: Sudden change of course? Bad look suppressed by head of BBC

clue.text: 'French parent and English' will gather sharp comment regarding descent

clue.text: Expert very well accommodating Irish backing out

blocks.note: V is the usual abbreviation for very

taken as written
'so' and 'well' both open a sentence as fillers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very well' reads as a phrase of approval but splits into two pieces either side of the Irish material.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is someone with outstanding technical skill, especially a brilliant musical performer.

clue.text: French attraction not having a lot of ale chilled

indicators.note: without having something you lack it, so those letters are taken away
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: FR is the abbreviation for French

the word missing its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: Two cuts happen: the short form of the beer is itself what gets removed from the attraction, leaving APPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Frappé describes a drink iced or served over shaved ice, so it is a culinary word for cooled.

clue.text: Part of garden in meaner bit of Brooklyn cased by agent

blocks.note: meaner as in baser or more contemptible
the first letter
a fed is an American federal agent, an FBI officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cased' suggests a criminal checking out a place; here it means enclosed, with the agent wrapped round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower bed is a planted patch within a garden, set aside for growing ornamental plants.

clue.text: Computer assistant in operating system is a godlike figure?

clue.text: Provoke line about Southern French composer

clue.text: Strange endless stories circulating in European Community

being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless stories' sounds like gossip that goes on forever, but it means the word loses its last letter before being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means obscure, understood only by a few insiders, and so odd or unusual to outsiders.

clue.text: Kept up refusal in accepting L is fifth letter

taken as written
